name: GetConsentio Cookie Banner – GDPR Cookie Consent
author: rovidevconsentio

sections.description:
Activate the plugin and your GDPR / ePrivacy cookie banner (cookie consent notice) is live. No account, no wizard, no external requests. The banner script is about 10 KB gzipped, ships inside the plugin and loads with defer, so your Core Web Vitals stay green, and it can block analytics and advertising scripts until the visitor actually consents.

Want more? Optionally connect a free GetConsentio account in one click to add a record of every consent (the proof GDPR asks you to keep), statistics, an automatic cookie declaration and rules by visitor country. Full documentation: getconsentio.com/docs.

Why site owners choose GetConsentio

  • Prior consent that really works (opt-in). Optional auto-block holds back known trackers until the visitor accepts, so you are not just showing a banner while cookies are already set.
  • Google Consent Mode v2. All four signals (ad_storage, analytics_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization) are set before your Google tags fire. Google Consent Mode is a Google feature; this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.
  • Works out of the box. The banner appears as soon as you activate the plugin, using your site name and your WordPress privacy policy page. No account required.
  • Private by default. Without an account nothing is sent to external servers: the script is served from your own site and each choice stays in the visitor’s browser.
  • Built-in scanner. One click checks your home page for well-known analytics and advertising services (Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Hotjar and more) and lets you block them until consent.
  • WP Consent API ready. If the WP Consent API plugin is active, the visitor’s choice is passed on so other plugins respect it.
  • EU opt-in and US opt-out. Choose GDPR (opt-in) or US-style opt-out, or let the country decide automatically (connected account).
  • Fast. About 10 KB gzipped, loaded with defer. No jQuery, no extra render-blocking requests.
  • Speaks your visitors’ language. Spanish, English, French, German, Italian and Portuguese, detected automatically from the visitor’s browser language (or country, with a connected account).
  • Proof of consent (connected account). Consent choices are logged in your GetConsentio dashboard, which is what regulators ask for when they ask for evidence.
  • Easy withdrawal of consent. A [consentio_preferences_link] shortcode adds a “Cookie settings” link anywhere.
  • One-click connection. Connect a GetConsentio account without copying keys around. Settings screen translated into Spanish, Italian, German, French and Portuguese.
  • Cookie declaration page (connected account). Add a live, always up to date cookie table to any page with the [consentio_cookie_declaration] shortcode.
  • Your look. Center or bottom position, light or dark theme, your accent color, your company name and cookie policy link.
  • Free. The banner is free without an account, and the GetConsentio account has a free plan; upgrade only if you need more sites or features.

Works with your stack

Standard WordPress script queue, so it works with any theme that calls wp_head(): Astra, GeneratePress, Divi, Elementor, Kadence, Block themes (Twenty Twenty-Five and newer), WooCommerce stores, and Site Kit / Google Analytics / Google Tag Manager / Meta Pixel setups. Add the banner once and it covers every page.

Who is it for?

Blogs, small businesses, agencies managing client sites, WooCommerce shops and any site in the EU, UK, Switzerland or with EU visitors that uses analytics, advertising or embedded media.

Not legal advice

A cookie banner helps with compliance but does not by itself make a site compliant. Review your cookie policy and privacy policy with a qualified adviser.

External services

Without an account (default) the plugin does not contact any external service. The banner script is served from your own site (assets/consentio.min.js, readable source in assets/consentio.js) and consent choices are stored only in the visitor’s browser.

If you choose to connect a GetConsentio account (by clicking “Connect with GetConsentio” or pasting a site key), the plugin uses the Consentio consent management service (getconsentio.com):

  • What it is and what it’s used for: Consentio is a cookie consent banner (CMP) service that keeps a record of each consent, statistics and the cookie declaration for your site.
  • What data is sent and when: from that moment, on every page load the banner script is loaded from https://getconsentio.com/consentio.min.js, configured with the site key and settings you enter under Settings → GetConsentio (company name, cookie policy URL, region, language, position, theme, categories). Once the visitor makes a choice, that choice (and, depending on your plan, technical data such as IP-derived country and browser user agent) is sent to and stored by getconsentio.com to keep a record of consent, as required by GDPR/CCPA and similar laws. While an account is connected, WordPress also asks getconsentio.com about once a day (sending only the site key) whether the account is on a paid plan, so the banner can be shown without GetConsentio branding. When you click “Connect with GetConsentio”, your site’s domain and the address of the plugin settings page are sent to getconsentio.com so the key can be returned to your site.
  • Terms and privacy policy: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the getconsentio-cookie-banner folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. That’s it: the banner is already showing on your site. Open it in a private window to see it.
  4. Optional: under Settings → GetConsentio set company name, cookie policy URL, region, language, position, theme and color.
  5. Optional: click Connect with GetConsentio to add consent records, statistics and the cookie declaration ([consentio_cookie_declaration]). Prefer to do it by hand? Create a key at getconsentio.com and paste it.
sections.faq:
Do I need a GetConsentio account?

No. The banner works as soon as you activate the plugin, with no account and no external requests. A free GetConsentio account is optional: it adds a server-side record of each consent (proof of consent), statistics, the automatic cookie declaration and rules by visitor country.

Is the plugin free? What do paid plans add?

The plugin and the banner are free, with no account and no limit on how many sites you use it on. A GetConsentio account adds a server-side record of every consent. Paid plans (prices without VAT) add downloadable proof of consent (CSV and JSON), a PDF compliance report and no GetConsentio branding: Pro is 9 € a month or 90 € a year for up to 3 websites, and Agency is 29 € a month or 290 € a year for up to 25 websites and 10 team seats. See the plans.

Does the banner show a credit link?

No, not by default. Under Settings → GetConsentio there is an optional Credit checkbox that adds a small “Powered by Consentio” link; it is off unless you tick it.

What is the difference between using it with and without an account?

Without an account the banner, script blocking and Consent Mode v2 all work, and each visitor’s choice is stored only in their own browser. With an account, each consent is also recorded in your GetConsentio dashboard so you can demonstrate it later, which GDPR expects you to be able to do.

Is it GDPR compliant?

It implements prior consent (opt-in) with real script blocking, granular categories and easy withdrawal, plus a log of each consent when you connect an account. Compliance also depends on your cookie policy and how you configure your tags; this is not legal advice.

Does it support Google Consent Mode v2?

Yes, with all four consent signals, set before Google tags load. Required for Google Ads and GA4 audiences in the EEA.

Does it block Google Analytics, Meta Pixel and other trackers until consent?

Enable Auto-block in the settings (or use Scan my home page → Block them until consent). Known trackers are then held back until the visitor accepts the relevant category: their script tags are neutralised before the page is sent, so the browser does not request them. Tags fired from inside Google Tag Manager are governed by Consent Mode instead.

Will it slow down my site?

No. The script is about 10 KB gzipped and loaded with defer.

Does it work with caching plugins (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache)?

Yes. The banner runs in the browser, so page caching does not affect it. The plugin marks its script so that optimizers (Autoptimize, WP-Optimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket and others) do not combine, delay or minify it, so it loads before your analytics tags. If you still see trackers firing before consent, add consentio.min.js to your optimizer’s JavaScript exclusion list and clear its cache.

Does it work with WooCommerce, Elementor, Divi or Gutenberg?

Yes. It uses the standard WordPress script queue, so it works with any theme or page builder.

The banner does not show on my site. What should I check?

  1. Under Settings → GetConsentio, make sure Legal region is not set to “No banner”. If you already accepted or rejected, the banner will not show again: use a private window.
  2. Open the site in a private window and clear your page cache / CDN cache.
  3. If you use an optimizer that delays or combines JavaScript, exclude the consentio script from it.
  4. The banner is intentionally not loaded inside the Customizer or page-builder editors; check the live site.

Does it work with the WP Consent API?

Yes. If the WP Consent API plugin is active, GetConsentio registers with it and passes on each visitor’s choice (statistics, marketing, preferences), so plugins that support that standard respect it.

How do I know which cookies my site uses?

Under Settings → GetConsentio, click Scan my home page. The plugin lists the well-known analytics and advertising services it finds and lets you block them until the visitor consents. It checks the home page only and cannot see tags loaded inside Google Tag Manager.

Can visitors change their choice later?

Yes. Add the [consentio_preferences_link] shortcode (for example in a footer widget or menu) to show a “Cookie settings” link that reopens the banner.

Can I show the cookie table on a page?

Yes, with a connected account. Use the [consentio_cookie_declaration] shortcode on any page or post.

Can I change the language or show it by country?

Yes. Choose a fixed language or the visitor’s browser language. Automatic by country needs a connected account.

What happens to my settings if I uninstall the plugin?

The plugin removes its saved settings on uninstall. Consent records stay in your GetConsentio account, where you can export them.

Where can I get help?

Use the support forum here, or write to hello@getconsentio.com.
sections.changelog:
1.6.2

  • New: the settings screen now explains what the paid plans add (proof of consent you can download, up to 3 or 25 websites) for business sites and agencies.
  • New: optional Credit checkbox to show a small “Powered by Consentio” link in the banner. It is off by default; nothing is shown unless you enable it.

1.6.1

  • Fix: optimizer plugins (Autoptimize, WP-Optimize and similar) could combine or delay the banner script so that trackers ran before it. The script now tells them to leave it alone, and the plugin registers its exclusions with the most popular optimizers. Tested with Autoptimize, WP-Optimize, LiteSpeed Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache and W3 Total Cache.

1.6.0

  • New: scanner on the settings screen. It checks your home page for well-known analytics and advertising services and offers to block them until consent. The check runs on your own site; nothing is sent to third parties.
  • Improved: auto-block is now much stricter. Known analytics and advertising scripts already present in the page are held back on the server, so the browser does not even request them before the visitor consents; the banner script loads first in the page when auto-block is on.
  • New: WP Consent API integration. When that plugin is active, consent choices are shared with it so other plugins can respect them.

1.5.0

  • New: the banner works as soon as you activate the plugin. No account needed and no external requests: the script is bundled with the plugin and choices are stored in the visitor’s browser.
  • Fix: sites connected to a paid GetConsentio plan now show the banner without the “Powered by Consentio” line.
  • The GetConsentio account is now optional. Connect it to add consent records, statistics, the cookie declaration and rules by visitor country.
  • Note for sites that had the plugin active without a site key: the banner will now be shown. Set Legal region to “No banner” if you do not want it yet.

1.4.1

  • One-click connect now requires HTTPS on your site (the button is hidden otherwise; you can still paste the key).
  • Added a small, dismissible review reminder shown to administrators after two weeks of use.

1.4.0

  • New: “Connect with GetConsentio” – create your free account or sign in and your site key is saved in WordPress automatically. No copying and pasting. A random one-time token protects the return trip.
  • Fix: connection parameters are now URL-encoded.

1.3.0

  • New: Consent Mode v2 is set to “denied” at the very top of the page (GDPR region) so Google tags added by other plugins can never run before the default is in place.
  • New: guided setup on the settings screen (3 steps while no key is set, “Banner active” status once it is), and a redirect to the settings page right after activation.
  • New: [consentio_preferences_link] shortcode – a “Cookie settings” link visitors can use to change or withdraw consent at any time.
  • New: admin screen translated into Spanish, Italian, German, French and Portuguese.
  • New: the cookie policy link defaults to your WordPress privacy policy page when left empty.
  • New: native color picker for the accent color; the site key is validated and a clear message appears if it looks wrong.
  • Improved: the banner no longer loads inside the Customizer or the Elementor, Beaver Builder, Divi and Bricks editors.
  • Security: configuration JSON is now encoded with JSON_HEX_TAG / JSON_HEX_AMP.

1.2.4

  • Settings page: the “Enter your site key” notice now links straight to the free sign-up so you can get a key in about a minute.

1.2.3

  • Plugin name no longer includes third-party product names (“Consent Mode”), per the Plugin Directory naming guidelines. Google Consent Mode v2 is still supported; it is a Google feature and this plugin is not affiliated with or endorsed by Google.
  • Readme: consistent settings page name (Settings → GetConsentio).

1.2.2

  • Fix: the banner script is now registered with a plain false (load in header) instead of an array argument that only WordPress 6.3+ understands, so it loads in the header on WordPress 5.8-6.2 as well (before it could end up in the footer there).

1.2.1

  • Settings screen strings translated from Spanish to English (source language), matching the readme and WordPress.org conventions.
  • Cookie declaration shortcode: the inline script that triggers Consentio.renderDeclaration() is now registered and enqueued via wp_register_script() / wp_add_inline_script() instead of being printed as a raw <script> tag in the shortcode output, and only loads on pages that actually use the shortcode.
  • Documented the plugin’s use of the Consentio external service (getconsentio.com) in this readme, with links to its Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.

1.2.0

  • Script now registered and enqueued via wp_register_script() / wp_enqueue_script() instead of a raw echo, per WordPress coding standards.
  • Bumped “Tested up to” to the current WordPress version.

1.1.0

  • Direct “Settings” link from the plugins list and a notice when the site key is missing.
  • Script cache-busting by version (?v=).
  • Stricter sanitization and an uninstall.php to clean up the option on uninstall.

1.0.0

  • First release: settings (site key, company, policy, region, language, position, theme, color, categories and auto-block), cookie declaration shortcode, and early injection in wp_head.
